airports: Charles M. Schultz Sonoma County Airport

en.title: FAA proposes $170,000 fine against Sonoma County Airport and $58,000 against Arapahoe Flight Club
en.summary: The FAA has proposed a $170,000 civil penalty against Sonoma County Airport for alleged aircraft rescue and firefighting and wildlife inspection violations, and a $58,000 penalty against Arapahoe Flight Club for alleged drug and alcohol testing violations. Both have 30 days to respond.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposes a $170,000 civil penalty against the Charles M. Schultz Sonoma County Airport (STS) in California for allegedly violating aircraft rescue and firefighting and wildlife inspection requirements. The agency alleges the airport did not provide the required personnel and vehicles for aircraft rescue and firefighting coverage for two passenger flights in March 2025, as required by its FAA-approved Airport Certification Manual, and did not notify the airline of the lack of coverage.

The FAA also alleges that, for one of those flights, the airport failed to perform runway inspections for deer and other wildlife before the first flight of the day, as required by its FAA-approved wildlife hazard management plan. Sonoma County Airport has 30 days after receiving the FAA's notice to respond to the agency.

In a separate action, the FAA proposes a $58,000 civil penalty against Arapahoe Flight Club of Colorado Springs, Colorado, for allegedly violating FAA drug and alcohol testing program regulations. The agency alleges the commercial air tour operator hired two pilots and two aircraft mechanics without conducting a pre-employment drug and alcohol test for each and receiving a verified negative drug test result, and allowed all four to perform safety-sensitive functions without adding them to its random drug and alcohol testing pool. The alleged violations occurred on various dates between May 2024 and September 2026, and Arapahoe has 30 days after receiving the FAA's notice to respond.

zh.title: FAA擬罰索諾瑪縣機場17萬美元、阿拉帕霍飛行俱樂部5.8萬美元
zh.summary: FAA擬對索諾瑪縣機場處以17萬美元民事罰款，指其涉嫌違反飛機救援與消防及野生動物檢查規定；另擬對阿拉帕霍飛行俱樂部處以5.8萬美元罰款，指其涉嫌違反藥物與酒精檢測規定。兩者皆有30天時間回覆。
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）擬對加州查爾斯·舒爾茨索諾瑪縣機場（STS）處以17萬美元民事罰款，指其涉嫌違反飛機救援與消防及野生動物檢查規定。FAA指稱，該機場未依其經FAA核准的機場認證手冊，為2025年3月的兩架次客運航班提供規定的救援與消防人力及車輛，也未通知航空公司缺乏保障。
FAA另指稱，該機場未依其經FAA核准的野生動物危害管理計畫，在其中一架次航班當日首班機起飛前執行跑道檢查，查看是否有鹿隻及其他野生動物。索諾瑪縣機場在收到FAA通知後有30天時間回覆。

在另一案中，FAA擬對科羅拉多州科羅拉多泉的阿拉帕霍飛行俱樂部處以5.8萬美元民事罰款，指其涉嫌違反FAA藥物與酒精檢測計畫規定。FAA指稱，這家商業空中遊覽業者聘用兩名飛行員與兩名飛機維修員時，未對每人進行職前藥物與酒精檢測並取得確認無陽性的檢測結果，且讓四人在未納入隨機藥物與酒精檢測名單的情況下執行安全敏感職務。相關涉嫌違規發生在2024年5月至2026年9月間的不同日期，阿拉帕霍在收到FAA通知後有30天時間回覆。

facts.claim: The FAA proposes a $170,000 civil penalty against the Charles M. Schultz Sonoma County Airport (STS) in California for allegedly violating aircraft rescue and firefighting and wildlife inspection requirements.

The FAA alleges STS did not provide the required personnel and vehicles for aircraft rescue and firefighting coverage for two passenger flights in March 2025 as required by its FAA approved Airport Certification Manual, nor did STS notify the airline of the lack of coverage.

The FAA alleges that for one of the flights, STS failed to perform runway inspections for deer and other wildlife before the first flight of the day as required by its FAA approved wildlife hazard management plan.
The FAA proposes a $58,000 civil penalty against Arapahoe Flight Club of Colorado Springs, Colorado, for allegedly violating FAA drug and alcohol testing program regulations.

The FAA alleges Arapahoe hired two pilots and two aircraft mechanics without conducting a pre-employment drug and alcohol test for each and receiving a verified negative drug test result, and allowed all four to perform safety-sensitive functions without adding them to its random drug and alcohol testing pool; the alleged violations occurred on various dates between May 2024 and September 2026.
Sonoma County Airport and Arapahoe Flight Club each have 30 days after receiving the FAA's notice to respond to the agency.
